text: Consumed-but-unpersisted approvals break the evidence chain. A skeptical review's top finding called the user's P7 decision-page ratification 'fabricated' — the submission was real, but the Monitor watcher read it via `decision-page.sh answer --consume` (which deletes the answer file) and the rulings lived only in conversation context. No durable artifact existed, so a fresh context could not distinguish 'never happened' from 'happened but unrecorded'. Root pattern: any consume/pop/ack-style read of an external decision (decision-page answers, Monitor events carrying user approvals, queue messages) must persist the payload to disk IMMEDIATELY, before acting on it. Fix that landed: style/sweep/20260727-simple-lang/vetted/p7-rulings.json + run-meta event. Candidate rule/hook: the decision-wizard skill's answer step could mandate a persist-on-consume line, or answer --consume could itself archive to <slug>.answer-archive.json.

What finally made a UI round land after several failed ones (owner: 'THIS is good enough'). Five moves, ranked by contribution: (1) ROOT-CAUSE OVER SYMPTOM - 'the page doesn't scroll' is structural, so the question was 'what does the shell expect from a page?' not 'which padding class?'. The shell's route handle had two contracts, layout:'list' (page owns an inner scroller) vs layout:'flow' (shell panel scrolls it); the page declared 'list' with no inner scroller so overflow had nowhere to go. One line. (2) COMPARE AGAINST SIBLINGS, DON'T JUDGE IN ISOLATION - 'look like the other pages' is a spec already written in the codebase: read the shared container CSS, read what two sibling routes declare, screenshot a sibling for a gutter comparison. This also separated the real remaining difference (this page now owns a scrollbar) from an imagined one. (3) INDUCE THE FAILING STATE - the default page fit on screen, which is exactly why the scroll bug survived multiple screenshots; adding 3 fields to force overflow then pressing End exposed it instantly. (4) TREAT THE COMPLAINT'S VOCABULARY AS DIAGNOSTIC - 'bad in visuals AND usability' is two axes, so the toolbar needed an interaction change (splitting Save from Save-as so a click's target is unambiguous), not only spacing. (5) DID IT INLINE - both delegated audit agents went idle without writing their reports; everything that landed was done in the browser by the main agent. THE MISS WORTH KEEPING: the evidence was in hand hours earlier - a full-page screenshot that stops mid-page IS the no-scroll bug - and it was rationalized away as 'an inner scroll container' instead of tested. An anomaly in your own evidence is a lead, not noise. TWO STANDING PRACTICES CONFIRMED: verify a delegated agent's artifact exists rather than trusting its 'done'/idle signal (the only reason 23 adversarial findings exist), and give reviewers source access - the audit that worked converted two pixel-level guesses into verdicts by grepping the JSX.
